title: Proton pump inhibitors for functional dyspepsia
authors: Pinto-Sanchez MI, Yuan Y, Hassan A, Bercik P, Moayyedi P
followUp: 2 to more than 6 weeks of treatment
population: 25 randomised trials in adults with functional dyspepsia comparing PPIs with placebo, H2-receptor antagonists or prokinetics; 17 of the 25 trials were sponsored or funded by a pharmaceutical company, 2 by an institutional grant, 8 gave no information
funder: Not read: the PubMed Central record holds the abstract, plain language summary and a PDF only, and the Cochrane Library page refused access.
authorConflicts: PM has consulted for or received speaker fees from Allergan, Shire and Lupin and received a research grant from Takeda, which sells a PPI; other authors none known.
result: PPI against placebo: relief of overall dyspepsia symptoms RR 0.88 (95% CI 0.82 to 0.94; 18 trials, 6172 participants; number needed to treat 11; moderate quality); against H2-receptor antagonists RR 0.88 (0.74 to 1.04; low quality); against prokinetics RR 0.89 (0.81 to 0.99; number needed to treat 16; low quality). No difference in the number of adverse events; specific adverse events were outside the scope of the review.
